model: PS-8 series extractive gas detector (Modbus TCP)
applies_to: New Cosmos PS-8 series pump-type gas detectors for semiconductor plants (up to 16 sensor channels) with Ethernet Modbus TCP, Instruction Manual for Communication GAE-180-00 (December 2024).
summary: The PS-8 is a New Cosmos pump-sampling gas detector for semiconductor process and flammable gases, holding up to 16 sensor units. Its Ethernet port is a Modbus TCP server with all data in holding registers. This map covers the integer gas readings, decimal points and flow for all 16 channels, relay states, heartbeat, alarm reset, clock, and the channel 1 settings block (other channels repeat every 101 registers).

addressing.note: Registers are printed as 40001-42984 with a relative (wire) address column; 40005 = relative address 4, confirmed by the function 03 example frame that reads 40005 with start address 0x0004.

source.title: PS-8 Series Gas Detector Instruction Manual for Communication
source.pages: p. 6 (TCP specs), pp. 16-18 (frame examples), pp. 21-37 (register maps)

notes: All 32-bit items are left out: the status and fault-detail DWords (40001-40004 per channel), and every IEEE-754 float (40126-40249 block, float settings). The manual gives float examples as "upper word" / "lower word" without saying which register address each sits at, so the word order cannot be settled from the source.

Character strings (serial number, tag and gas names) are also left out: the manual puts the 2nd character in the upper byte and the 1st in the lower byte, an order the string type here cannot express.
Gas readings are integers: real value = raw / 10^decimal (decimal register 0-3). Example from the source: 20.9 vol% = 209 with decimal 1.

The channel 1 settings block (40301-40397) repeats for channels 2-16 at +101 registers per channel (channel 2 starts at 40402). Grouped arrays for all 16 channels also exist at 42301-42984; only the concentration and unit arrays are listed here.
Factory IP address is 192.168.0.101; the specification table allows at most 2 connected units. Writing to reserved or read-only registers is ignored; reading reserved registers returns 0.

integration.summary: Connect over Ethernet to 192.168.0.101 port 502 and read holding registers 0-111 (seven words per sensor) with function 03; use the integer concentration and decimal registers for each channel.
integration.enable: Menu > Device Information > Modbus: select TCP/IP. Set IP and subnet (or DHCP) under Device Information.
quirks: Reading starting at a reserved register gives an illegal-address error; reserved registers inside a longer read return 0.
Date/time must be read or written as all three words together.
setup: No proxy; the built-in web page at the IP shows live channel data for a quick check.
gotchas: Maintenance mode masks the alarm and fault bits of the status words.
Settings marked change notification set a bit in 40124; clear it by writing 0.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
note: Re-typed from the manufacturer's public documentation (see source) and verified against it. Registers vary by firmware and options; verify against the live device before writing.
